newsitem.title: USA: Briggs & Stratton cites demand shift for net slide.
newsitem.headline: Briggs & Stratton cites demand shift for net slide.

text.p: Briggs & Stratton Corp said Wednesday a shift by lawn and garden equipment makers in their product schedules was a factor behind a 30-percent drop in net income and a nine-percent sales dip in the second quarter, which ended December 1996.
The company said the shift by manufacturers resulted in lower demand for its engines in summer and fall.

The company reported profits of $16.7 million in the period, compared with $23.9 million a year ago. Sales reached $299.7 million, down from $329 million in the second quarter of 1996, Briggs & Stratton said.
The company makes engines for lawn and garden equipment.
Its shares closed down 1/4 Wednesday at 45.
